title: purchase-requisition-risk-tiering-sla-and-escalation-2026
author: Priya Nair
body:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the purchase requisition risk-tiering model, target SLAs for approvals and purchase order issuance, and the escalation ladder for exceptions. It standardizes how requisitions flow from request to commitment so finance, procurement, and legal can reliably map commitments to revenue recognition and vendor onboarding steps.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference business units when creating purchase requisitions and committing to vendor spend, including Hosted, Dedicated, and Private product teams.
- Includes SaaS subscriptions, cloud spend, hardware purchases, contract services, and multi-year commitments.
- Excludes petty cash and expense reports (handled in expense policy).

Definitions:
- Requisition (Req): Initial request by a requester to purchase goods/services.
- Commitment: Binding financial obligation created when a PO is issued or contract signed.
- Risk Tier: Categorization of requisitions by commercial, compliance, and financial risk.
- SLA: Target time interval for each approval step.

Risk Tiering Matrix (determinants and examples):
| Tier | Total Value (net ARR equivalent) | Key Risk Flags | Typical Approval Path | Notes |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 - Low | < $10k | Standard SaaS, single-year, pre-approved vendor list | Manager -> Finance automated approval (48h) | Fast-track, auto-PO where applicable |
| Tier 2 - Moderate | $10k - $100k | Multi-year <=2yrs, new vendor, minor IP/data access | Manager -> Procurement -> Finance (72h) | Standard SOW, credit check, basic vendor form |
| Tier 3 - High | $100k - $1M | Multi-year >2yrs, custom work, data residency, or requiring SLA/insurance | Manager -> Procurement -> Legal -> Finance (7 business days) | Requires contract review, security questionnaire |
| Tier 4 - Strategic | > $1M or material vendor | Any strategic vendor, significant security/compliance or offshore data flow | Exec sponsor + Procurement -> Legal -> CFO (variable; target 14 business days) | Requires board-level notification for > $5M or strategic platform commitments |

Requisition lifecycle and SLAs (targets):
1. Request creation: requester fills requisition template in Procurement Portal; checklists populate for required attachments (SOW, MSA, security questionnaire).
2. Manager review: 24–48 hours to confirm need and budget center.
3. Procurement intake: triage and assign risk tier within 48 hours of manager approval.
4. Legal intake (if required): review kickoff within 1 business day after procurement assignment.
5. Contract review cycle: target 5 business days for Tier 2, 7 business days for Tier 3, 14 business days for Tier 4 (measured from first legal review assignment to redline complete).
6. Finance approval and PO issuance: target 24–48 hours after contract sign-off or approved requisition for auto-POs.

Approval routing rules (examples and exceptions):
- Auto-approvals: Items on the pre-approved catalog and Tier 1 requisitions under $2k are auto-approved by Finance if budget center has available funds.
- Delegated approvals: Managers may delegate approvals to designated deputies during leaves; delegation must be recorded in the Procurement Portal.
- Cross-charge and internal transfers: If the spend is internal redistribution (e.g., cloud chargeback), follow internal chargeback form and finance acceptance before PO.

Escalation ladder and steps (operational procedure):
1. If any step misses SLA, the current owner must escalate to the next-level owner within 24 hours, documenting the reason in the requisition notes.
2. Escalation path by missed SLA: Procurement Lead -> Procurement Manager -> Finance Ops Lead -> Head of Procurement -> CFO (for Tier 4 or > $500k).
3. For legal bottlenecks longer than SLA, legal assigns an owner and must provide a 24-hour remediation plan or suggest an interim mitigation (e.g., redline with conditional sign-off, playbook-approved fallback clause).
4. For security/compliance blockers, Security Review Board is convened within 48 hours by Procurement Lead.

Vendor due diligence checklist (minimum items by tier):
- Tier 1: W-9/Entity name, verification in vendor registry.
- Tier 2: Vendor questionnaire, basic SOC/ISO attestation if available, commercial references.
- Tier 3: Full security questionnaire, legal entity verification, insurance certificates, data flow map, and KYC.
- Tier 4: In-depth security assessment, on-site or detailed architecture review, exec sponsor sign-off, and backup vendor contingency plan.

Integration with Contracts, Revenue Recognition, and Billing:
- All commitments created via PO or executed contract must be recorded in the Contract Management System (CMS) with the following tags: vendor_id, contract_value, start_date, end_date, commitment_type. These tags are required for RevRec automation.
- Mapping examples: one-time professional services = recognized as % completion per SOW; multi-year committed capacity (Dedicated) = amortized monthly; committed discounts = recorded as deferred revenue adjustment by Finance RevRec team.
- Trigger rules: PO issued without an executed MSA for a Tier 3/4 vendor triggers legal hold and deferred PO state; Finance will not recognize revenue or bill customers on any deliverables tied to non-executed contractual dependencies.

PO JSON example (for automation):
{
  "po_id": "PO-2026-00451",
  "vendor_id": "V-9982",
  "amount": "125000",
  "currency": "USD",
  "tier": "3",
  "sow_reference": "SOW-2026-07",
  "contract_id": "CMS-2026-3342",
  "business_unit": "dedicated-capacity",
  "approval_history": ["mgr:2026-01-12T09:12Z","procurement:2026-01-15T13:20Z","legal:2026-01-20T15:42Z","finance:2026-01-21T10:03Z"]
}

(Automation note: approval_history is an array of strings in the CMS; logging timestamps enables SLA measurement and invoice matching.)

Monitoring, KPIs, and dashboards:
- Key metrics to track weekly: median time to triage, median legal review time by tier, percentage of requisitions meeting SLA, number of escalations by reason, vendor onboarding lead time.
- Targets: 90% of Tier 1 approved within 72 hours; 75% of Tier 2 approved within 7 days; 60% of Tier 3 within 14 days.
- Dashboards: Procurement Portal should expose filters for business_unit, tier, pending_days, and approval_owner. Finance and Legal each have a dedicated RevRec/Contract dashboard for contract tagging completeness (>98% target).

Roles and responsibilities (quick reference):
- Requester: Completes requisition, attaches SOW/requirements.
- Manager: Validates need, confirms budget center, first approver.
- Procurement: Triage, vendor diligence, routing to Legal/Finance, SLA steward.
- Legal: Contract review, redline ownership, risk mitigation.
- Finance: Budget validation, PO issuance, RevRec alignment.
- Security: Assessment owner for data-handling vendors.

Exception handling examples (common scenarios):
- Rush procurement for pilot requiring >$100k within 3 business days: require Exec sponsor email, Procurement-approved expedited intake, and Legal fast-track checklist.
- Vendor refuses standard MSA change that affects RevRec: Procurement escalates to CFO, Legal documents risk, Finance may require escrow or alternate billing terms.

Change control and continuous improvement:
- Procurement will run a quarterly SLA retrospective. Action items are tracked in the procurement backlog and prioritized by impact to RevRec and go-live blockers.
- Any changes to tier thresholds or approval owners must be approved by Head of Procurement and CFO and published with a 30-day notice.

Appendix A — Requisition template checklist (fields):
- Requester name; date; business_unit; budget_center; cost_center_code; vendor_name; vendor_entity_id; estimated_amount; currency; justification; required_by_date; attachments (SOW, security questionnaire, PO template).

Appendix B — CLI snippet for procurement portal (example):
# Create requisition (example CLI)
redwood-proc req create \n  --requester "alice@redwood.ai" \n  --business-unit "dedicated-capacity" \n  --vendor "V-9982" \n  --amount 125000 \n  --currency USD \n  --tier 3 \n  --attachments ./SOW.pdf,./security-questionnaire.pdf

Contacts and owners:
- Procurement operations (primary): procurement-ops@redwood.ai
- Legal intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai
- Finance PO operations: finance-po@redwood.ai
- Escalation: head-of-procurement@redwood.ai
